Design effect of a cluster sample, from the intraclass correlation

Source: R/plan.R
deff_cluster.Rd

The design effect of taking m rows from each cluster, for plan_size() before a pilot has measured one with deff(): 1 + (m - 1) * icc, with icc the intraclass correlation of the measure, the correlation between two rows of one cluster (Kish 1965). Rows of one cluster tend to be alike, so each row taken from a cluster already sampled adds less than a row from a new cluster would, and the more alike they are and the more taken from each, the larger the design effect.

Usage

deff_cluster(m, icc)

Arguments

m

Rows taken from each cluster, 1 or more. With one row a cluster, the design effect is 1 whatever icc is.

icc

Intraclass correlation, from a pilot or a published study of the same measure, between -1 / (m - 1) and 1. A negative one, rows of a cluster less alike than rows taken at random, gives a design effect below 1.

Value

The design effect, a number. m and icc may be vectors, recycled to a common length, and give one design effect per pair.

Details

The formula assumes every cluster gives the same number of rows, drawn by simple random sampling of clusters. plan_size() counts rows, so a plan of n rows in clusters of m takes ceiling(n / m) clusters, and the "Where the formula comes from" section of plan_size() explains why a few clusters call for more than the plan.

References

Kish, L. (1965). Survey Sampling. Wiley.

See also

plan_size(), deff() to measure the design effect of a past sample.

Examples

deff_cluster(m = 10, icc = 0.05)
#> [1] 1.45

# Rows to draw, and the clusters of ten rows that hold them
p <- plan_size(margin = 5, sd = 40, N = 20000,
               deff = deff_cluster(m = 10, icc = 0.05))
p$n
#> [1] 351
ceiling(p$n / 10)
#> [1] 36

# Takes of 5, 10 and 20 rows a cluster, side by side
plan_size(margin = 5, sd = 40, N = 20000,
          deff = deff_cluster(m = c(5, 10, 20), icc = 0.05))
#>     n n_effective margin level     N deff response target spread  p capped
#> 1 291         291      5  0.95 20000 1.20        1   mean     40 NA  FALSE
#> 2 351         351      5  0.95 20000 1.45        1   mean     40 NA  FALSE
#> 3 469         469      5  0.95 20000 1.95        1   mean     40 NA  FALSE
#>   short raised n_needed
#> 1 FALSE  FALSE      291
#> 2 FALSE  FALSE      351
#> 3 FALSE  FALSE      469
